t: Listen to a talk in a psychology class.
Psychologists often describe memory as three connected systems.
It takes in a huge amount of information from our eyes and ears, but it holds that information for only about a second.
If we pay attention to something, it moves into short-term memory.
Short-term memory can hold only a small number of items, about seven, and only for around twenty seconds unless we keep repeating them.
Think about the last time someone told you a phone number.
You probably repeated it to yourself until you could dial it, and then it was gone.
Its capacity seems to be practically unlimited, and information can stay there for years, even a lifetime.
Getting information into long-term memory usually requires connecting it to things we already know.
